source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party/press summaries describe export strategy of manufacturing certain products exclusively in India for global distribution and producing components for other Hitachi Energy factories worldwide, with export orders from US, Europe, APAC, South Asia and Africa. No explicit 'China+1' phrase found in sources retrieved.

govt_capex.evidence: Press/analyst commentary cites government-driven state transmission capex of INR 3.4 lakh crore over next five years fueling 8-9% annual market growth for high-voltage solutions; order backlog (~INR 32,222 crore Q1 FY27) attributed to India's power grid buildout, renewable integration, and data center expansion. No explicit revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party summaries note transformer-segment input materials (transformer oil, electric steel, copper, insulation) comprise ~80% of total input for that segment; not confirmed as total-company raw-material % of revenue, left null.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (~25-30% of total) spread across SAARC/SE Asia, Europe, US, Africa; company reported both forex gains and losses in recent quarters indicating unhedged/partially hedged exposure, no explicit hedging policy % found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source reporting indicates Finolex Cables revamped export team, growing export revenue from ~Rs30cr to ~Rs52cr; exports only ~1% of FY25 turnover with target to reach 2-3% over two years. No explicit China+1/diversification framing found.

rural.evidence: Secondary sources citing company commentary state Finolex has strong foothold in urban/semi-urban markets and is expanding into rural markets, with ~5,000 authorised channel partners and 200,000+ retail touchpoints across 554 districts (FY22-23 data). No rural revenue percentage disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary/analyst commentary describes government infrastructure push (roads, railways, housing, rural electrification, BharatNet, Smart Cities) as key demand driver; electrical wires & cables segment (~85% of revenue) also serves real estate/construction. No specific government-capex revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports estimated at only ~1% of FY25 turnover per secondary sources; no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy found.

rural.evidence: Industry/media commentary states rural sales account for roughly one-third of Royal Enfield's total sales, with rural demand growth outpacing urban; company expanding studio outlets into Tier-2/3 towns and states like Bihar, Odisha, and the North-East to deepen rural penetration.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors reported among ~20 companies approved as a 'Champion OEM' under the Auto PLI Scheme. No revenue/incentive amount specific to Eicher found; unclear whether approval sits at Eicher Motors/Royal Enfield level or its VECV commercial-vehicle JV.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB Group President & CEO stated (Jan 2025, Business Today) India is being developed as an 'export hub to support other geographies,' expected to become ABB's third-largest market within 3-4 years; ABB India follows 'local for local' with >85% of products sold in India manufactured domestically, contributing ~10-11% of ABB's global export volumes, with >US$230m invested over the past decade to build India as a global manufacturing hub. No explicit 'China+1' phrase found.

govt_capex.evidence: Multiple sources describe ABB India as beneficiary of sustained government capex in infrastructure, railways (traction/auxiliary converter orders), power T&D, metro rail, data centers, and renewables, with 'large orders' up 20% in CY2024 partly driven by railways and data centers. No specific revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: An older ABB India annual report (CY2019) disclosed commodity hedging of copper/aluminum/silver at ~90% hedge ratio via OTC contracts; no current raw-material %-of-revenue figure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: No current disclosure of USD-denominated revenue % or hedging policy located; an older AR (CY2019) referenced hedging of CHF exposure via forward contracts.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found of ABB India participating in a PLI scheme; core segments (electrification, robotics, motion, process automation) are not among primary PLI-covered sectors.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial data (interest coverage ~25.4x FY24 vs 13.3x FY23, debt-to-equity ~0.0, net debt-to-equity ~-0.27 by FY25) indicates minimal/no debt and net-cash position, so floating-rate liability exposure likely immaterial; no explicit floating-vs-fixed split located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Press/analyst commentary indicates ENA (agri-derived) and glass packaging together account for roughly half of raw material costs, with glass bottle cost inflation ~12-17% cited as margin pressure; no petroleum/crude-linked input percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: India accounts for ~99.6% of net sales implying minimal foreign-currency revenue exposure; no explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy located.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported (via third-party summary) to use a natural hedge, offsetting foreign-currency payables against receivables, with selective use of financial instruments for residual FX risk; revenues/expenses denominated in USD, EUR, GBP and CAD.
inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party summary citing CARE Ratings press release; exact policy wording not independently confirmed from primary filing.

pli_scheme.evidence: Reported as one of the domestic pharma companies approved under Group B of the Govt of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals; company-specific revenue contribution not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived summary indicates Power Solutions business grew partly on 'higher exports' and Powertrain Solutions growth aided by 'an increase in export sales.' No explicit China+1/diversification framing found; ~69% of exports go to Robert Bosch Germany (intra-group transfers), not evidence of China+1-driven customer wins.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~8.3% of FY2024-25 net sales) predominantly manufactured-goods shipments to other Bosch group companies; ~69% of exports go to Robert Bosch Germany implying EUR-linked exposure may be more material than USD, but no explicit currency split or hedging policy located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Per search-derived summary: 'Bosch had applied for the Auto PLI scheme and the application has been selected.' Also references Government's PLI/DLI/ISM schemes underpinning strategic investments. Related group entity Bosch Automotive Electronics India received separate Auto-PLI approval for ECU manufacturing (~USD 91.8M) — a distinct legal entity from listed Bosch Limited.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Coforge hedges foreign currency risk on highly probable forecasted revenue using Foreign Currency Forward Contracts designated as Cash Flow Hedges; earnings-call commentary also references a shift toward balance sheet hedges and natural hedges, reducing reliance on cash flow hedge contracts.
inr_exposure.evidence: Derived from third-party summaries of Coforge financial disclosures/earnings-call commentary; exact AR note text not directly verified (primary AR PDF unreachable in this session).

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' framing found. Netweb's disclosed narrative is domestic import-substitution/'Make in India' manufacturing: inaugurated a high-end computing servers/storage/switch manufacturing facility in Faridabad; MeitY Secretary quoted on strategic importance of domestic manufacturing. Framed around import substitution for India's own procurement market (Class-I local supplier preference) rather than global supply-chain diversification away from China for export growth. Export share small (~5-9% of revenue per third-party estimates).

govt_capex.evidence: Third-party market commentary (unverified) claimed government + PSU customers together account for roughly 58% of revenue, and that Netweb holds Class-I supplier status under India's Public Procurement Preference for Make in India mandate. Left null since figure could not be confirmed from primary source within fetch budget.

crude_exposure.evidence: Only qualitative commentary found (analyst note on raising inventory levels in 4QFY26 to battle rising raw material prices); no disclosed raw-material/component cost % of revenue or COGS.

pli_scheme.evidence: Confirmed beneficiary: Netweb Technologies India Ltd received a Production Linked Incentive of INR ~5.94 crore under the Govt of India's PLI 2.0 Scheme for IT Hardware, for period July 1 2023 to March 31 2024. Company is a select Indian OEM eligible under PLI 2.0 for IT Hardware/networking/telecom products, effective May 2023. Incentive as % of total revenue not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source summaries of Anthem's IPO disclosures/management commentary describe an explicit China-plus-one positioning: 'Over 80% of Anthem's revenue is derived from exports, primarily to the US, Europe, and China... While most Indian pharma companies rely on China for 60-70% of their inputs, Anthem's dependence is below 20%, and this independence took over a decade to build and has become a key differentiator.' Management framed the company as a direct China alternative for global pharma clients: 'We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones.' NOTE: quotes drawn from IPO-period news coverage (Moneycontrol/Business Standard), not directly read from AR/RHP (unreachable in this environment).

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary states Anthem's raw-material dependence on China is 'below 20%' vs 60-70% typical for Indian pharma peers, attributed to decade-long supply-chain diversification. Describes China-sourced share of raw materials, not raw materials as % of revenue/COGS; could not verify against actual AR/RHP.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely to US/Europe pharma/biotech clients) reported at roughly 80% of revenue per secondary sources implying material USD/foreign-currency exposure, but no explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage or hedging policy located.

Global Health Ltd (Medanta) Q3 FY2025 press release (Feb 4, 2025): revenue from international patients increased 14.3% y-o-y to Rs. 541 million against total income of Rs. 9,595 million in Q3 FY25 (~5.6% of total income); Q4 FY25 report cited international patient revenue ~Rs. 55.7 crore, ~6% of quarterly total revenue, up 17% y-o-y.

rural.evidence: Third-party commentary describes Radico dominating semi-urban and rural segments via value brands (e.g., 8PM) with pan-India network of 60,000+ retail outlets emphasizing rural/semi-urban penetration; no disclosed rural revenue percentage found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Broker notes indicate raw material costs linked to grain, ENA and packaging material prices; grain inflation cut Q4 FY24 gross margin by ~490bps YoY. Sitapur grain-based distillery (commissioned FY25) shifts input linkage from ENA toward grain, pre-tax benefit of Rs 6-7/litre. No raw-material % of revenue disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (~9-10% of total) implies some foreign-currency exposure, including exports to Middle East/Gulf and Africa, but no USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure located.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Radico Khaitan participating in a PLI scheme; alcoholic beverages are not a PLI-covered sector in India.

china_plus_one.evidence: European business grew 15.4% YoY in FY25 with EBITDA growth of 20.9%, outperforming industry; European subsidiaries secured EUR40m in new orders including Volkswagen and BMW EV/hybrid wins; company focus is exporting gravity die casting (GDC) and low-pressure die casting (LPDC) solutions to Europe and North America. No explicit China+1/diversification framing found.

Third-party analyst commentary (not verified against primary AR, inaccessible): 'Navin Fluorine has gained from a trend in which pharmaceutical corporations shift some production to India rather than China... reflects the broader China Plus One strategy.' CDMO business (fastest-growing segment) revenue rose ~82% YoY to INR 180 crore in Q1 FY26, driven by 'sustained engagement with leading innovator pharma clients' seeking supply-chain diversification.

rural.evidence: Secondary sources (news coverage of Titan/Tanishq commentary) note Tier-2/Tier-3 towns outperforming Tier-1 and cite deeper penetration into Tier 3-5 towns as a stated growth strategy, but no explicit rural/Tier-2-3 revenue percentage was found; primary AR PDF could not be accessed to confirm any disclosed figure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Secondary sources note Titan added ~Rs 3,500 crore of long-term borrowings (NCDs and term loans) in FY24, but no floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not crude-linked; Titan's dominant raw material is gold (jewellery) rather than crude/petro-based inputs. No specific raw-material cost percentage disclosed in sources accessed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Press/management commentary describes Titan following a near-100% gold hedging strategy with ~120-day forward procurement visibility to manage gold price volatility; could not verify against primary Annual Report text.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company has a growing International Business segment (GCC/Middle East and North America jewellery and watches) reported in quarterly disclosures, but full-year FY25 international revenue as % of total was not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention found of Titan participating in India's PLI scheme; jewellery/watches/eyewear are not sectors covered under the PLI framework.

govt_capex.evidence: Company manufactures power transmission/distribution equipment (transformers, switchgear) sold largely to state DISCOMs and government/utility customers; secondary sources reference India's RDSS (~Rs 3 lakh crore DISCOM modernization scheme) and rising power-sector capex as a tailwind for SEIL, but no annual-report-disclosed revenue % tied to government capex was located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources note exposure to copper, aluminium, steel, resins and plastics as key input costs for electrical equipment/enclosures, but no annual-report-disclosed raw-material % located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party earnings-call/broker summaries report Divi's benefiting from 'higher outsourcing trend and the China+1 strategy,' building capacity 'in a few more niche APIs... in the backdrop of China plus one opportunities and upcoming opportunity size of approximately US$20 billion in molecules going off-patent over FY23-25.' Also: 'Divi's multi-source procurement strategy spans suppliers from across the US, European Union, Middle East and Asia, while promoting domestic sourcing,' and 'US Biosecure Act tailwinds are creating new RFPs from global Big Pharma.' Not verified against primary AR text (PDF fetch blocked).

crude_exposure.evidence: Search-derived summary of concall/financials: 'Material consumption was 40% of sales revenue for 9M FY25.' Not broken out by crude-linked solvent vs. other raw materials; not confirmed against primary AR notes.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~87-90% of sales across recent quarters) presumed largely USD-denominated given US/Europe customer base, but no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure located. 9M FY25 forex gain reported ~INR 38 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found confirming Divi's Laboratories as an approved beneficiary under the pharma API/KSM PLI scheme; searches on approved beneficiary lists surfaced other companies (Aurobindo, Sun Pharma, Dr Reddy's, Cipla) but not Divi's. Divi's business is predominantly custom synthesis/CRAMS rather than bulk-drug molecules typically covered under PLI.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analyst coverage (not confirmed against primary AR): 'global buyers seeking certified suppliers and implementing China+1 sourcing strategies... KBL's standing as the world's only NABL-accredited pump manufacturer gives it a measurable edge in both domestic mega-project contracts and international export markets.' KBL recently secured NABL accreditation for its Hydraulic Research Centre pump-testing lab, cited as a competitive differentiator for international buyers diversifying away from China. Group reportedly exports to 70+ countries across Africa, SE Asia and Europe.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural revenue % disclosure found. Proxy data: 'Small Pumps' (mini, monobloc, submersible borewell, dewatering pumps — primarily agriculture-use) at approximately 24% of one quarter's sales. FY24-25 order wins under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) for pumps across MP, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, UP and J&K, plus irrigation wins from Narmada Valley Development Authority and UP Irrigation Department.

govt_capex.evidence: Water Resource Management/Irrigation is a core business vertical alongside large infrastructure projects (Water Supply, Power Plants, Irrigation). FY24-25 order wins tied to Jal Jeevan Mission and state irrigation departments/NVDA documented in press coverage; AMRUT 2.0 cited as further growth driver. No explicit % of total revenue attributable to government/infra capex found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/overseas-subsidiary revenue (SPP UK, SPP Inc USA, SPP Mena, KBTL Thailand/Singapore, Dutch Group) reported at ~INR 1,603 crore in FY25 against consolidated revenue of ~INR 4,492-4,564 crore (~35%), implying meaningful foreign-currency exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme participation found for Kirloskar Pneumatic Company Ltd (White Goods/ACs PLI) — a separate, affiliated Kirloskar Group listed entity, NOT Kirloskar Brothers Ltd. No PLI participation found for Kirloskar Brothers Ltd itself.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary reporting describes Sona Comstar pursuing geographic diversification across North America, Europe and India to reduce concentration risk (e.g. new Mexico plant to cater to growing EV demand in North America, highest-ever order book of Rs262bn including a major North American OEM order). No explicit China+1 framing tying revenue/order growth to customers diversifying away from China found. Notably, the company is simultaneously moving INTO China (JV talks with BYD, Jinnaite Machinery JV attempt) to serve Chinese OEMs, which complicates a simple China+1-beneficiary framing.

pli_scheme.evidence: Per press coverage, Sona Comstar became the first auto component supplier to receive Auto PLI certification (Feb 2024), initially for a hub-wheel-drive motor for electric two-wheelers, filed seven applications across products; later received PLI certification for three additional EV traction motor products (Aug 2025). Specific revenue contribution from PLI incentives not found.
